c2_berit_note.title: A note in the book
c2_berit_note.text: Between two pages of the old book there is a note in thin brown ink: “Rest the field. Rest yourself. — B.” You read it twice. Then you look at your hands.

c2_k_rest.text: The note in the book flutters in the wind. It says what it always says.

pages.text: The river barge brings a letter. Mei from the barge nods, hands it over and rows on. The writing is round and quick: your mother's.
“Come home before the frost, my love. The house is small, but the table is long. Your cousin asks after you.” You fold the letter very small. The frost is far away. Isn't it?

c2_walls.title: Crooked walls
c2_walls.text: The walls of the cottage stand. You built them alone, and it shows. One leans a little to the left. You step back, look at them for a long time, and decide that they are perfect.

pages.text: A boy waits at your gate with a basket of herbs bigger than his arms. “You're the Moonedge one,” he says. “You used to carry a bucket bigger than you.” You did.
“Why is that wall crooked? Does it hurt when you hammer? Did you know sage is good for a cough?” He asks too many questions. You find, to your surprise, that you do not mind.

c2_stumps.title: Too many stumps
c2_stumps.text: So many stumps, for such a small farm. Their tops are clean and flat. Someone cut the forest back, long ago, and nobody planted anything in its place.

c2_lark.title: A visitor on the new road

pages.text: A man walks up the new gravel road as if he had always walked it. He sits on your fence and watches you work. “Lark,” he says. Then he says nothing at all for a while.
You stack a crate. He stacks one too, a little crooked. “Probably fine,” he says. It is. Mostly. When you look again, the fence is empty and both crates are still standing.
You clear the last black beam from the barn. Then you stop. The burn does not start at the roof, where lightning would strike. It starts low, in the corner where the hay was kept.
You sit back on your heels. Lightning does not start low. Something else began this. You do not know what. And you find that you do not want to know. Not yet.

c2_compost.title: A tidy pit
c2_compost.text: Behind the barn is a compost pit, clean and dry, its edges squared with flat stones. Someone cared about this. Scratched on the lid: “Feed the ground and it feeds you. — B.”

c2_cottage.title: A roof before the frost
c2_cottage.text: A real roof, before the frost. You sit under it while the first rain taps on the tiles. Then you take a sheet of paper and write home: “I'm staying a bit longer.” Your hand shakes only a little.

pages.text: Something very slow is crossing the yard. A tortoise, moving like a stone that has decided to travel. She goes straight to the pond and sits down where the spring first rose.
You sit down beside her and wait. The pond fills a little, then a little more. Nothing is hurried. And the second line of the old rhyme comes back to you: “Slow shell keeps the water clean.”

c2_hook.title: A blackened hook
c2_hook.text: In the new barn frame you find an old iron hook. It is black with soot, and it was made to hold a lantern. “If it was not lightning,” you think, “then what?” You hang the hook back up. Carefully.

pages.text: Back in the room, somebody has fallen asleep on the floor. “Did you find out who started it?” asks Minena. “Not then,” you say. “I didn't want to.”
“And the man on the fence? Was he funny?” “Very.” “Was that good?” “It made him hard to talk to,” you say, and nobody understands. That is all right.
